In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the uptake and degradation in vivo of vitamin D binding proteins (DBPs) and their complexes with actin in the rat.
the study of vitamin D binding proteins (DBPs) in the circulation.
the role of DBP in vitamin D homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DBP-actins are cleared from plasma at the rate of 0.4% of injected dose per min.
the binding of actin enhances the clearance and catabolism rate of DBP in vivo in the liver, but not in the kidney.
the DBP-actomyosin complex is cleared faster from the blood stream than DBP, and that DBP is cleared faster from blood stream than albumin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the uptake and degradation rate of a protein is dependent on the binding to a ligand.
DBP-actins are rapidly cleared from the circulation and taken up by the organs, where they are degraded.
DBP-actins are taken up by liver cells and then degraded in lysosomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DBP is cleared from plasma at different rates depending on the type of protein bound to it.
we have developed a method to study the catabolisms of proteins in vivo.
DBP-actins are cleared faster than DBP from circulation.
